rationale: Everything today is about GLP-1 medicines, and the slate leans on what our numbers say works. Tirzepatide muscle is our best evergreen lane (122 and 98 views). Calm warnings about gray-market 'Reta' are our top Short (128). Titles that name a drug and ask 'did X beat Y?' also do well. The long-form had to survive the fact-check, so it's an evergreen deep-dive on strength training while taking tirzepatide. It rests on peer-reviewed sources: the SURMOUNT-1 body-scan substudy, WHO and US activity guidelines, and the 2025 joint nutrition advisory. Today's news only sets up the intro. S1 is a spin-off of L1 to pull viewers to the long video. The breaking and emerging stories go into Shorts: the Penn/JAMA Network Open study of Reddit posts on retatrutide (emerging, flagged caution, run as a 'what's confirmed vs not' myth-correction), and the ACHIEVE-3 pill-vs-pill head-to-head (rising). The carousel is the open-enrollment coverage checklist (rising, seasonal, a list people save). Mix: about 40% rising or emerging (S3, C1), 40% evergreen with a timely hook (L1, S1) and 20% myth-busting (S2). No pillar is used more than twice. Muscle is the only body system that appears twice; the others are GI side effects, pills and insurance. The 'stopping' lane (weak on YouTube) and scare-style eye and NAION topics (low-performing) are left out on purpose. Every piece carries the prescriber line, no dosing, no switching or stopping advice, and no seller or sourcing details.

pieces.topic: Strength training while taking tirzepatide (Mounjaro/Zepbound): how much of the weight lost is lean mass, why muscle matters for metabolic health and function, and a guideline-based plan to start
pieces.angle: Evergreen 'where to start' deep-dive. Hook: muscle preservation is in the news (UNC Health '5 habits on a GLP-1', Oct 15). Body: (1) what lean mass vs fat mass means and how a DXA scan measures it, noting that lean mass isn't pure muscle; (2) SURMOUNT-1 DXA substudy: about three-quarters of the weight lost was fat mass, in adults with obesity, or overweight with a weight-related condition, without diabetes. Give per-arm figures and the timeframe from the paper; (3) why some lean-mass loss happens with any weight loss, including diet-only and bariatric comparisons from the literature, labelled as separate studies; (4) what the guidelines recommend: muscle-strengthening activity at least 2 days a week (WHO / US Physical Activity Guidelines), starting gently, a beginner progression using bodyweight, bands and machines; (5) protein at each meal from a variety of foods, per the 2025 joint nutrition advisory, unless your clinician has told you to limit protein (e.g. kidney disease); (6) training around common GI side effects: eat slowly, fluids unless you've been told to limit fluids; (7) questions for your prescriber, a dietitian or a physical therapist. Habits are 'recommended', never 'proven on tirzepatide'. No dosing. Close with the full prescriber line.
pieces.working_title: Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) and Muscle: Where to Start Strength Training
pieces.why: Our strongest evergreen lane (122/98 views) with tirzepatide in the title, built on peer-reviewed sources and guidelines that hold up to the long-form fact-check.

pieces.topic: Losing weight on tirzepatide? 3 ways to start strength training
pieces.angle: Direct 'you' hook, named drug, numbered promise, answered with data by about 10 s: 'In the SURMOUNT-1 body-scan substudy (adults with obesity, or overweight with a weight-related condition, without diabetes), about three-quarters of the weight lost was fat.' Then 3 guideline-recommended starts: (1) muscle-strengthening at least 2 days a week, starting gently; (2) a protein food at each meal unless your clinician has told you to limit protein; (3) progress slowly with bodyweight or bands. 'Recommended', not 'proven on tirzepatide'. One GI side-effect line, the prescriber line, and 'follow for more' unless L1 is already published. 170 words or fewer.

pieces.topic: AI analysis of about 150,000 Reddit posts on gray-market 'retatrutide': increased appetite was the most reported symptom, not the GI effects seen in the trials (Penn, JAMA Network Open, Oct 2026)
pieces.angle: Retatrutide on Reddit: why people's reported side effects don't match the trial. Penn researchers (JAMA Network Open, Oct 14, 2026) used AI to analyse about 149,000 Reddit posts and comments from about 39,000 users. The most reported symptom was increased appetite (17.1%), not the mostly-GI pattern seen in the Phase 2 trial. On screen: 'self-reported · not a trial · product contents unknown'. Dated status: investigational, not approved anywhere as of Oct 2026; Lilly says it plans to submit to FDA in Q1 2027. Safer route: ask your prescriber about approved options or a clinical trial.
pieces.working_title: Retatrutide on Reddit: Why Reported Side Effects Don't Match the Trial #shorts
pieces.why: A peer-reviewed new angle on our best-performing lane (bootleg Reta, 128 views) with low competition. It's a contrarian-but-true correction, and the radar's caution flag is handled with an evidence-first framing. | fact-check: Verified: Penn engineers' cross-sectional study, 'Self-Reported Adverse Effects Among Social Media Users Taking Nonapproved Retatrutide', JAMA Netw Open, published online Oct 14, 2026. It analysed 148,640 Reddit posts AND comments from 38,936 users in 27 communities, 2021–2025. Top reports: increased appetite 17.1%, fatigue 15.2%, increased energy 12.4%, nausea 11.6%. Fixes: (1) Say 'about 149,000 posts and comments from about 39,000 users', not '150,000 posts'. (2) The paper compares with the Phase 2 trial, so say 'the Phase 2 trial'. Phase 3 TRIUMPH results have been reported since (Jul 2026), so don't imply the Phase 2 trial is the only trial data. (3) The status is outdated. Lilly has said it plans to submit to FDA in Q1 2027 (per Lilly's TRIUMPH announcement, Jul 2026). Use Lilly's exact wording and date it: 'investigational, not approved anywhere as of Oct 2026'. (4) GI symptoms were still common, just not dominant. Don't say GI effects 'weren't reported'. (5) The authors' caution is that products may not contain real retatrutide. Attribute it to them and don't overstate it. Don't amplify alarming symptom lists (e.g. '129 symptoms'). No vials, sellers, doses or sourcing. Cite the FDA unapproved-GLP-1 page directly. Prescriber line, and suggest clinical trials as the legitimate route.

pieces.topic: Orforglipron (Foundayo) vs the semaglutide pill head to head: ACHIEVE-3 in adults with type 2 diabetes
pieces.angle: Did orforglipron beat the semaglutide pill in type 2 diabetes? In ACHIEVE-3 (52 weeks, adults with T2D on metformin), Lilly reported that A1C fell by 2.2 points on orforglipron 36 mg vs 1.4 on oral semaglutide 14 mg (Rybelsus), and weight fell by 9.2% vs 5.3%. Orforglipron has no food or water timing rules; the semaglutide pill does ('follow your label'). Dated status: orforglipron (Foundayo) is approved for weight management (Apr 1, 2026) but not yet for type 2 diabetes as of Oct 2026. Common side effects are GI (nausea, diarrhea). Don't switch on your own. Prescriber line.
pieces.working_title: Orforglipron vs Semaglutide Pill: Who Lost More in Type 2 Diabetes? #shorts
pieces.why: A rising 'did X beat Y?' story about two named drugs people already search for. The pill Short format works (53 views, 52 reach), and the comparison is a real randomized head-to-head. | fact-check: Verified via Lilly's ACHIEVE-3 release: 52 weeks, n=1,698, adults with T2D on metformin, 4 arms (orforglipron 12 and 36 mg; oral semaglutide 7 and 14 mg). A1C −1.9% / −2.2% vs −1.1% / −1.4%. Weight −9.2% (36 mg) vs −5.3% (oral semaglutide 14 mg). Credit as 'Lilly reported' unless a peer-reviewed paper is cited. Needed changes: (1) Label status. Foundayo is approved (Apr 1, 2026) for chronic weight management only. Lilly planned a T2D submission by end of Q2 2026. As of the latest sources I found, the T2D indication is NOT confirmed approved, so say 'not yet approved for type 2 diabetes as of Oct 2026 (submitted, per Lilly)' unless the FDA label shows otherwise. Don't imply it's a T2D option today. (2) Drop the indirect 25 mg comparison: it's a crowded number and a scope risk (the playbook warns about crowded numbers). (3) The Wegovy pill (approved Dec 22, 2025) is semaglutide 25 mg for weight, a different product and dose from the 14 mg Rybelsus-type arm in the trial. Call the comparator 'oral semaglutide 14 mg (the diabetes pill, Rybelsus)', not 'the Wegovy pill'. (4) A1C units are percentage points. Include one GI line, no verdict on which is better for you, and no switching advice. Lead with A1C, the primary endpoint, and frame weight as a secondary endpoint.

pieces.topic: US open enrollment and GLP-1 coverage for 2027: employers are adding and dropping coverage (Walmart $0 for some employees with T2D; Vox on coverage drops)
pieces.angle: Short (not a carousel), US-only: 'Open enrollment: 5 questions to ask about tirzepatide or semaglutide coverage for 2027.' Hook dated Oct 2026: some employers are adding coverage (e.g. Walmart: $0 for some GLP-1s for employees with type 2 diabetes, with prior authorization, per Becker's, Oct 13, 2026), while others are dropping it (cite a verified primary survey or article). Then 5 quick questions: covered for T2D, weight, or both? Prior authorization and what documentation it needs? Step therapy? Tier and out-of-pocket cost? Do official manufacturer savings programs apply to your plan type (they often exclude government plans)? Never compounded, gray-market or no-prescription online sources. Don't stop or change your medicine on your own. Ask your prescriber or pharmacist. Disclaimer plus the full prescriber line.
pieces.working_title: Open Enrollment & GLP-1s: 5 Coverage Questions to Ask Your Plan (US)
pieces.why: Seasonal search cycle (open enrollment runs to about Nov 6), and a practical list that suits the save-and-share carousel format. | fact-check: The topic is useful and safe, and the Walmart fact checks out: Becker's Payer, confirmed Oct 13, 2026. For 2027, some GLP-1s are $0 for employees with type 2 diabetes, with a new prior authorization, and the plan still covers T2D only. Write exactly that, never 'Walmart covers GLP-1s for weight loss'. The Vox piece on coverage drops wasn't verified in this screen, so the writer must open it and quote it accurately, or replace it with a primary employer-survey source (e.g. KFF/Mercer). Format problem: carousels are proven dead (all 17 reached 0–3 accounts), and the playbook says to rebuild good carousel topics as Shorts. Change it to a Short. The topic also has no named drug, which underperforms, so name tirzepatide/semaglutide in the hook. Manufacturer savings programs: official programs only. Say they often exclude government plans (Medicare/Medicaid), check terms, and promote no specific program. Keep 'US only', the slide/scene on avoiding compounded and gray-market sources (no seller names), 'don't stop or change your medicine on your own', the disclaimer and the prescriber line.
